bib.title: SpQR: A Sparse-Quantized Representation for Near-Lossless LLM Weight Compression

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; raw sensitivity heatmap figures (Fig 10, 11) are images with only axis ticks as text.

question: Can LLM weights be quantized to 3-4 bits per parameter with under 1% relative perplexity loss, including for 7-13B models, while still giving faster-than-fp16 token generation?
hypothesis: Quantization error is concentrated in structured and unstructured sensitive weights; storing those in 16-bit and the rest in small quantized groups with quantized statistics gives near-lossless compression.
contributions: Analysis of weight quantization sensitivity showing row, column, attention-head, rotary and unstructured outlier patterns in LLaMA-65B
SpQR format: bilevel quantization with very small groups plus a CSR-like sparse set of 16-bit outliers
Extended GPTQ-style PTQ algorithm that isolates outliers during quantization
Efficient GPU decoding and a sparse-matrix algorithm for the outliers, faster than 16-bit inference

method.summary: Post-training quantization extending GPTQ: per-weight sensitivity from the inverse Hessian selects ~1% outliers kept in 16-bit (CSR-like storage); other weights get 3-4 bit codes in groups of 8-32 whose scales and zero points are themselves quantized to 3 bits in groups of 16. Evaluated by perplexity and zero-shot accuracy on LLaMA, Falcon, OPT, plus A100 token-generation speed.

parameters.bs, bz: 3 bits each for quantized scale and zero
parameters.beta1: 8-32 weights (group size); 16 in the 30B near-lossless config; 8 in the size-controlled 3-bit setup
parameters.beta2: 16 in Sec 4.1 and Table 5 baseline; 64 in size-controlled setup in Sec 5
parameters.tau: outlier threshold, tuned in [0.1, 1.0] by binary search, step 0.05; most configs 0.1-0.45; 0.1 for LLaMA-30B near-lossless
parameters.outlier_rate: under 1% in all SpQR evals; optimal 0.2-0.5% in App E
parameters.outlier_storage: 16-bit value + 16-bit column index per outlier, plus 32-bit per-row count; 32.03 to 32.1 bits per outlier
parameters.other_flags: act order permutation, fit quantizer without outliers, non-integer zero point, no sign requirement on min/max

other.quantization_time: around 4.5 hours for 65B on A100 and about 6 on A6000
other.quantization_calibration_size: not stated for Section 5 (128 x 2048 tokens only for the Sec 3.2 analysis)

results.claim: SpQR reaches within 1% of fp16 perplexity on LLaMA at 4.63 to 4.71 average bits.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B/13B/30B/65B, SpQR near-lossless configs, single seed, calibrated on RedPajama
results.quote: SpQR with 4.6 to 4.71 bits per parameter approaches the non-quantized models with at most 1% margin of error for all models

results.claim: At about 3.9 bits SpQR still beats 4-bit GPTQ and RTN on LLaMA-7B Wiki2 but is not within 1% (5.87 vs fp16 5.68).
results.table: Table 1, LLaMA 7B, row SpQR 3.94, column Wiki2 (5.87); GPTQ 6.13; RTN 6.43; fp16 5.68
results.note: 5.87 is about 3.3% above 5.68, so the sub-4-bit configs are not near-lossless.

results.claim: Falcon-7B and 40B reach within 1% perplexity at under 4.5 bits.
results.quote: SpQR reaches performances within 1% of the perplexity with less than 4.5 bits per parameter.

results.claim: At 4 bits SpQR halves the error relative to 16-bit compared with GPTQ.
results.setup: LLaMA and Falcon, 4-bit-sized comparison against GPTQ
results.quote: For 4-bit, SpQR halves the error relative to the 16-bit baseline compared to GPTQ.

results.claim: Optimized SpQR kernel generates faster than fp16 on a single A100, speedup roughly 20-30% in the text.
results.setup: A100, batch size 1, LLaMA 7B, generate 100 tokens from scratch
results.table: Table 4, rows scratch, columns fp16 7B (47 ± 2.3) and SpQR (optimized) 7B (57 ± 2.4)
results.note: Abstract says 15% speedup; Section 1 and 5 say 20-30%. From Table 4 ratios: scratch 7B 57/47 = 1.21, 13B 44/37 = 1.19, 30B 22/19 = 1.16; prefix 1024 7B 55/46, 13B 37/31, 30B 22/17 = 1.29. 65B fp16 is OOM on the A100 so no comparison.

results.claim: Standard PyTorch sparse matmul is not faster than 16-bit; the custom kernel gives about 20-30% speedup.
results.quote: our specialized sparse matrix multiplication algorithm yields speedups of about 20-30%.

results.claim: Abstract: 33B model on a single 24 GB consumer GPU at 15% speedup.
results.setup: No 24 GB GPU timing or 33B model appears in the experiments; speed measured on A100, LLaMA sizes 7/13/30/65B; Table 9 recommends 30B at b~4.5 for 24 GB RTX4090
results.note: Abstract text: 'run 33B parameter LLM on a single 24 GB consumer GPU without any performance degradation at 15% speedup'. Not backed by a measurement in the body.

results.claim: 1% of weights can account for over 75% of the total quantization error in some layers.
results.setup: LLaMA-65B sensitivity analysis, 3-bit GPTQ, some cases
results.quote: In some cases, 1% of the weights account for over 75% of the total quantization error.

results.claim: SpQR compresses to as little as 3.36 bits with a better size-quality tradeoff.
results.setup: Discussion; no table row at 3.36 (Table 5 min effective is 3.051 without outliers, 3.45-3.52 in zero-shot tables)
results.quote: We achieve even better quality-size-tradeoff when compressing to as little as 3.36 bits

results.claim: Zero-shot average at 3.45 bits is below fp16 on LLaMA-7B (60.96 vs 61.492) while the 4.63-bit config matches (61.460).
results.table: Table 7, LLaMA 7B, row SpQR 3.45, column Avg score (60.960); fp16 61.492; SpQR 4.63 61.460

results.claim: Small groups with 3-bit quantized statistics beat larger groups with 16-bit statistics at the same size (LLaMA-65B).
results.table: Table 3, rows 3-bit statistics (3.74, 3.63 bits) and 16-bit statistics (3.84, 3.67 bits)

results.claim: Unstructured outliers reduce perplexity faster than row outliers or the Dettmers & Zettlemoyer column criterion.
results.setup: LLaMA-65B, 3-bit SpQR, Fig 4 (values read from plot only)
results.quote: unstructured outliers reduce perplexity significantly faster than their row counterpart and the criterion of [DZ22]

results.claim: Optimal outlier fraction is 0.2-0.5%; higher-precision weights beat very small groups or large outlier fractions.
results.setup: Appendix E configuration sweep, WikiText2 vs average bits (Fig 8)
results.quote: In our experiments optimal fraction of outliers is 0.2-0.5% depending on the model and groupsize.

results.claim: Seed variation is much smaller than the gap between SpQR and baselines.
Average memory per outlier is about 32 bits and the size formula is b = bw + (bs+bz)/beta1 + 64/(beta1 beta2) + 32 ro.
results.quote: This results in an average storage cost of 32.03 to 32.1 bits per sensitive weight.

results.claim: Quantization takes around 4.5 hours for LLaMA-65B on an A100.
results.quote: Our implementation takes around 4.5 hours on the largest model size (65B)

limits: Only perplexity and zero-shot accuracy are measured; generation quality is not evaluated (authors concede, Sec 6); Appendix I has only 4 qualitative greedy samples.
Sparse outlier multiply is not fused with the quantized dense multiply (Sec 6).
Speed measured only on a single A100 at batch size 1; no 24 GB GPU or 33B model timing despite the abstract claim.
Main results use one fixed seed; Appendix H seed check is only LLaMA-65B at 3.625 bits.
Near-lossless (1%) holds only at about 4.6-4.75 bits; the 3.4-3.9 bit configs lose more (e.g. LLaMA-7B 5.87 vs 5.68).
Calibration set size for the main quantization runs is not stated; Hessian regularizer lambda value not stated.
Outliers cost ~32 bits each and are not grouped; quantized copies of outliers are retained (future work).
Document is arXiv v1 (June 2023); the PDF does not state a venue.
